description: Fictional English scanner training handover with corrected counts and settings, spelled acronyms, an eight-second pause and a checkback before completion.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Let's walk through the shared scanner before the afternoon session. We'll use ordinary sample pages today, and we'll check the saved file before calling the handover complete.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Good. I've used a flatbed scanner before, but I haven't used this document feeder or its saved settings.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The document feeder is called the A D F. First remove clips and staples, then place the pages face up with their top edges pointing into the feeder.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Face up, top edges first, with clips removed. I should check both sides before loading the stack.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Exactly. For this exercise, choose grayscale at three hundred dots per inch. The color setting at six hundred makes much larger files and isn't needed for these handouts.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I was about to choose color at six hundred. I'll change both settings before I press the scan button.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: We have eighteen pages in the sample stack. The handwritten note looks like eighty, but that's wrong. Count the sheets now so we can compare the result later.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I've counted eighteen sheets. The display also says eighteen pages are ready, so those two counts agree.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Now choose a searchable P D F and leave automatic rotation enabled. Don't delete any pages just because they appear blank in the small preview.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Automatic rotation stays on, and I'll keep every page until we've checked the full file. What's our first check after scanning?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: We'll open the full file, confirm the page count, and read the first and last pages. I'm going to check which destination folder has write access.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I'll wait here and leave the settings alone. I haven't started scanning or changed the destination yet.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I'm back. The training folder accepts new files, so use that destination. Give the file the title Training Sample and add today's date in the date field.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Training folder, title Training Sample, and today's date in its own field. I'll start the scan now.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The progress bar has stopped, but wait for the green completion message. A stopped bar by itself doesn't tell us whether the file was actually saved.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The green message is showing now. I'll open the saved file rather than relying on the preview window.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Please count all eighteen pages and check that the last paragraph is readable. If a page is missing, keep the original file and report the problem before rescanning.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: All eighteen pages are there, and the first and last pages are readable. I can also select a sentence.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That confirms the searchable text is present. Tomorrow, try a separate three page sample yourself, but use this same checklist and ask if any status message is unclear.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Three pages for tomorrow's practice, with the same checklist. I won't replace today's file with that new sample.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I'll update the written checklist by Wednesday at noon, including the corrected page count and both scan settings. The handover record should link to today's verified sample.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I'll complete my practice check by Thursday at ten and report the result. If saving fails, I'll stop and ask.
